mechanism_narrative: The recent rebound in WORKPLACES after a three-week decline signals more weekday trips and lunch-time errands, which should lift RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks relative to the prior four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains below its last-4-week mean over the next 28 days despite WORKPLACES staying at or above -16% on weekly means.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL stays elevated while TRANSIT remains deeply negative, more activity shifts to local, drive-to shopping and dining, which raises RETAIL_REC within one to two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT stays below -40% for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase above its last-4-week average within 14 days after TRANSIT remains below -40% for two straight weeks and RESIDENTIAL stays above +5%.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp upswing in PARKS mobility indicates improving weather and outdoor visitation, which spills over into nearby retail and recreation visits and lifts RETAIL_REC over the following four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises by at least 15 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to move above its prior 28-day mean in the month after a PARKS increase of 15 points or more from one week to the next.

mechanism_narrative: A synchronized recovery in GROCERY_PHARM and WORKPLACES indicates relaxed mobility constraints and broader consumer activity, which should raise RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC stays below its last-4-week mean even when GROCERY_PHARM and WORKPLACES both rise for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT begins to recover from a deep negative level, commuters regain access to shopping corridors and leisure districts, producing higher RETAIL_REC within one week.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises by 3 points or more week-on-week from a level below -40%
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase in the week after TRANSIT posts a week-on-week gain of at least 3 points from below -40%.

mechanism_narrative: When WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both remain depressed, discretionary shopping is delayed rather than displaced, so RETAIL_REC weakens over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES stays below -15% and TRANSIT stays below -40% for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above its prior 28-day mean during the next 28 days while both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT remain below the stated thresholds.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in RESIDENTIAL indicates people are spending less time at home and more time out, which should translate into more retail visits and a higher RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not exceed its last-4-week mean within 14 days while RESIDENTIAL falls from its current level.

mechanism_narrative: If PARKS rebound while RETAIL_REC is still depressed, the leisure rebound will pull shopping trips back first through combined outing behavior, causing RETAIL_REC to improve over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS turns up after a weekly trough below -30%
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains flat or declines over the next 28 days even though PARKS reverses upward from below -30% and stays above its prior week.
